messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach detected for /v1/stream (hosted) — threshold 3s, p99=9.2s, p95=2.8s. Trace sample: https://grafana.redwood.example/r/streaming-p99

sanjay: i'm on it. grabbing graphs and recent deploys.

olivia (oncall): thanks. i'll handle customer comms if we confirm impact. which regions? any errors?

maria: seeing an increase in streaming stalls starting ~09:12 UTC in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. clients report long pauses between SSE chunks. no 5xx spike yet.

max: deploy at 08:50 UTC (revision f2a1). linking deploy bot output:
```
devops-bot: deploy inference-runtime/f2a1 -> us-west-2 succeeded (08:50 UTC)
```

maria: capture from proxy logs (nginx sidecar) with repeated upstream timeouts:
```
[09:14:02] upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream
[09:14:07] client unexpectedly closed connection
```

qa-ops: client telemetry shows small chunk sizes get buffered for ~5-10s before flush; suggests proxy buffering/backpressure rather than model slowdowns.

sanjay: ok so model seems to be producing tokens but proxy or envoy is buffering. can someone confirm model-side tail latency? p99 token-gen for last hour?

max: model-side p99 token latency stable ~80ms. so not runtime. network/proxy layer looks suspect.

maria: reproducer: open websocket to /v1/stream?session=test and watch chunk intervals. I see bursts then long pauses. tcp dump shows packets held until buffer fills.

sanjay: let's triage fast: 1) disable proxy buffering for streaming paths, 2) increase proxy_read_timeout, 3) scale streaming pods, 4) enable fallback non-streaming route for critical customers.

olivia (oncall): i'm patching the customer-facing status: "Degraded streaming; generation continues but chunk delivery may be delayed. Team investigating." will post to customers affected with estimated ETA 30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

max: changing nginx sidecar config to `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 120s;` on the /v1/stream location. pushing a configmap update now.

devops-bot: rolling configmap update to 4 sidecar pods in us-west-2 (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%)

maria: canary applied, i see immediate improvement on that pod: chunk flushes every ~120-200ms. p99 decreased from 9s -> 1.9s for that subset.

sanjay: good. start accelerating rollout. kubectl scale deploy inference-stream --replicas=6 -n prod
```
kubectl scale deployment inference-stream -n prod --replicas=6
```

max: scaling done. autoscaler had been at 3. pods coming up in ~40s.

olivia (oncall): documenting mitigation for incident timeline. customer comms updated: pushing note to status page and to support threads.

qa-ops: note — some clients still use old edge proxy with `proxy_buffering on` in our CDN; we need to invalidate config there too. pinging CDN infra.

devops-bot: CDN edge config change requested (ticket #INC-4319).

maria: also seeing some long-lived websocket connections that get paused due to client-side backpressure (slow readers). that's contributing to connection saturation on some proxies. we should add connection-count-based circuit breaker per upstream to avoid head-of-line.

sanjay: short-term: increase max downstream connections and enable downstream connection limit per worker to avoid head-of-line. longer-term: implement per-client concurrency and backpressure metrics.

olivia (oncall): any customer-specific severity? should we page account owners?

maria: touched customers: 8 high-volume customers on streaming tier. two reported visible UX stalls. i've opened support threads and tagged account team.

max: will roll the same sidecar config to eu-west-1 now. starting canary.

sanjay: monitoring: add temporary alert for streaming chunk delay > 2s for p95 so we can auto-detect regressions post-fix.

devops-bot: alert rule created: streaming.chunk_delay.p95 > 2s for 15m -> page oncall.

maria: eu-west canary shows same improvement. full rollout complete. p99 across regions down to 1.2s, p95 ~0.45s.

olivia (oncall): marking customer impact as "degraded" -> "partial mitigation in place" in status update.

qa-ops: recommend follow-ups: 1) audit CDN/proxy default buffering flags, 2) add gating check in canary pipeline to detect proxy-buffered responses, 3) add streaming-specific e2e tests with head-of-line/backpressure simulation.

sanjay: agreed. owners: maria -> incident postmortem and mitigation writeup, max -> rollout and infra config PR, qa-ops -> e2e tests + acceptance criteria, olivia -> customer comms + stakeholder timeline.

olivia (oncall): handing off to day oncall @sanjay for final verification; i'll follow up with account teams.

sanjay: taking handoff. will keep watch for 1 hour and then request incident close if stable.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident commander: sanjay. Severity: Sev2. Start: 1760501234. Mitigation applied: proxy buffering disabled on streaming path, scaled streams, CDN ticket opened.

maria: collecting logs and traces for postmortem; adding example of affected client chunk timings to the incident repo.

max: PR for sidecar default config opened: https://git.redwood.example/p/infer-sidecar/pull/189 (includes test plan).

qa-ops: creating e2e test ticket: QAE-1023 (simulate slow reader + high concurrency).

olivia (oncall): final note to stakeholders: immediate mitigation applied, customers notified, postmortem assigned. closing communication loop later today. :white_check_mark:

sanjay: closing loop in 1h if metrics remain stable. thanks everyone.
